current.title: Most Billionaires
current.prompt: Rank US states by the total number of resident billionaires on the Forbes 400 list.
current.disclaimer: Billionaires counted by their primary state of residence, not their business's HQ state. DC not included (source omits it).
current.trivia: Roughly two out of every three Forbes 400 members live in just five states.

findings.detail: Value string format is inconsistent across tied entries. Some tied entries carry '(tied)' suffix, others do not: rank 15 AR='5 billionaires' but MN/OH='5 billionaires (tied)'; rank 20 MO='3 billionaires' but NC/OR/WI/WY='3 billionaires (tied)'; rank 25 AZ='2 billionaires' vs others '2 billionaires (tied)'; rank 30 AL='1 billionaire' vs others '1 billionaire (tied)'. Also singular/plural switches ('billionaire' vs 'billionaires').

current.title: Most Federally-Owned Public Land
current.prompt: Rank US states by percentage of total land area owned by the federal government.
current.disclaimer: Includes BLM, USFS, NPS, FWS, and DoD holdings; expressed as a percent of the state's total land area. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: Nevada is over 80% federally owned — a legacy of Bureau of Land Management holdings across the Great Basin.

findings.detail: DC listed at r51 with 24.7%. Actual federal ownership of DC land is very high (federal buildings, National Mall, monuments) — CRS reports typically exclude DC or show ~28%+. Regardless, 24.7% is inconsistent with rank 51 (last place); at that value DC should rank around 13-14, above HI (19.4%). This is both a sort-inversion and a bucket/rank fact error.

current.title: Most Native American Reservation Land Area
current.prompt: Name the US states with the most Native American reservation and trust land area.
current.disclaimer: Total federal trust and reservation acreage held for tribes and individuals; excludes Alaska Native Corporation lands (ANCSA) which have a different legal status. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: Arizona edges Alaska because most Alaska Native land was converted to corporate ownership under the 1971 ANCSA settlement rather than held as reservations.

findings.detail: Disclaimer says 'excludes Alaska Native Corporation lands (ANCSA)' but AK's rank 33 value '0.001M acres (Metlakatla only)' inconsistently adds a per-row qualifier not applied to other states. If ANCSA exclusion is uniform, the Metlakatla note is redundant; if AK's number is materially different, it belongs in the disclaimer.

current.title: Most Retail Sales per Capita
current.prompt: Rank US states (and DC) by highest per-capita retail sales.
current.disclaimer: Total retail sales divided by resident population; low-population, tourism-heavy states punch above their weight. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: New Hampshire's rate is inflated by Massachusetts shoppers crossing the border to avoid sales tax.

findings.detail: Values decrease by exactly $200 across almost all ranks from ~r10 onward ($19,000, $18,900, $18,700, $18,500, $18,300 ... $10,500). Uniform $200 stepping across 40+ states is not consistent with real Census retail-sales-per-capita data; values appear synthesized.

current.title: Largest Asian Population Share
current.prompt: Which US states have the largest Asian population share (alone or in combination)?
current.disclaimer: Asian alone or in combination with one or more other races. Includes Washington DC.

findings.detail: Tie at rank 8 uses '8.1% (tied)' for VA but plain '8.1%' for MA. Inconsistent tie-suffix formatting within the same question.

current.title: Most Electric Vehicle Registrations
current.prompt: Name the US states with the most registered plug-in electric vehicles (BEVs).
current.disclaimer: Counts light-duty battery-electric vehicles registered in the state; excludes plug-in hybrids in some tallies. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: California alone accounts for roughly 37% of all registered electric vehicles in the United States.

findings.detail: Prompt says 'plug-in electric vehicles (BEVs)' — 'plug-in' typically includes PHEVs while BEV means battery-electric only. Disclaimer says 'excludes plug-in hybrids in some tallies', which further hedges. Should specify BEV-only or plug-in (BEV+PHEV) consistently.

current.title: Cloudiest States (Fewest Sunny Days)
current.prompt: Rank the US states by cloudiest skies — states with the fewest average clear or sunny days per year (rank 1 = cloudiest).
current.disclaimer: Rank 1 is the cloudiest state. Based on mean number of overcast days per NOAA/NWS station normals. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: Seattle averages only about 71 clear days per year — but famously receives less annual rainfall than New York City despite its reputation.

findings.detail: Prompt says 'fewest average clear or sunny days per year (rank 1 = cloudiest)' but values are reported as 'cloudy days/yr'. The disclaimer refers to 'mean number of overcast days' while the source name is 'Mean Number of Clear Days'. Player is asked to rank by cloudy days but source metric per its title is clear days — inverse of value shown. Metric definition is inconsistent between prompt, disclaimer, source, and value label.

current.title: Driest States (Least Annual Precipitation)
current.prompt: Rank the US states with the lowest average annual precipitation, by statewide average.
current.disclaimer: Rank 1 is the driest state (lowest inches per year). Statewide averages, not local extremes. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: Nevada is the driest US state — parts of the Amargosa Desert receive under 3 inches per year, drier than many places in the Sahara.

findings.detail: See paired 'Wettest States' finding — the two lists disagree on many statewide 1991-2020 NOAA normals (NV, WY, CO, ND, ID, SD, MN, NY, WI, MI, IA, WA, IL, OH, MO, VT, VA, ME, DE, NJ, MA, NC, and more). Same source is cited for both. At least one of the two questions has bad values.

current.title: Highest Peak Elevation
current.prompt: Rank the US states by the elevation of their highest natural point (USGS).
current.disclaimer: All top-10 state high points are in the West except (technically) they all are — the highest peak east of the Mississippi is Mount Mitchell in North Carolina at 6,684 ft, which doesn't crack the top 15. Includes Washington DC.
current.trivia: Denali (Alaska) at 20,310 ft is the highest point in North America.

findings.detail: Disclaimer text is garbled/self-contradictory: 'All top-10 state high points are in the West except (technically) they all are'. Reads as an unfinished edit. Should be clarified (e.g., 'All top-10 state high points are in the West' or clarify the caveat).
